topic: Scangos, Chang & Krystal (2021): Closed-Loop Amygdala-Guided Brain Pacemaker for Severe Depression
visual_mode_reason: Stages the 2021 UCSF 10-day intracranial stereo-EEG mapping suite and Responsive Neurostimulation (RNS) closed-loop implant with a Contained Living 4-Color 3D Brain cutaway of amygdala gamma bursts triggering 6-second ventral capsule/ventral striatum pulses.

primary_case.place: UCSF Weill Institute for Neurosciences, University of California, San Francisco
primary_case.summary: Katherine Scangos, Edward Chang, Andrew Krystal, and colleagues (Nature Medicine, Oct 2021) mapped a 36-year-old woman ('Sarah') with severe treatment-resistant depression using 10 days of multi-site intracranial stereo-EEG, discovering a right-amygdala gamma biomarker that predicted symptom spikes with 87% accuracy and triggered a closed-loop ventral striatum pacemaker (~300 six-second pulses/day) that dropped her MADRS depression score from 36 to 10!

core_facts.fact: In Scangos, Khambhati, Chang & Krystal (2021 Nature Medicine), 10 days of continuous 10-lead intracranial stereo-EEG mapping in a 36-year-old woman with severe treatment-resistant depression identified bilateral amygdala high-frequency gamma power (30–110 Hz) as a personalized neural biomarker that classified high vs low symptom severity with 87 percent cross-validated accuracy.

Delivering brief 6-second bursts of 100 Hz, 1 mA electrical stimulation to the right ventral capsule/ventral striatum (VC/VS) exclusively when right amygdala gamma power crossed threshold suppressed pathologically elevated amygdala gamma activity and acutely relieved depressive distress without conscious paresthesia.

The implanted NeuroPace RNS closed-loop device delivered approximately 300 six-second stimulation bursts per day (totalling roughly 30 minutes of daily stimulation, capped to stop before 8:00 p.m. to protect sleep) rather than 24-hour continuous open-loop stimulation.

The patient's Montgomery-Åsberg Depression Rating Scale (MADRS) score dropped from 36 out of 54 at pre-surgical baseline to 14 within 12 days of closed-loop activation and achieved clinical remission at 10 (a 72 percent reduction) sustained across 15 months of follow-up.

Daily visual-analog depression severity ratings (VAS-D) fell from 77 out of 100 before closed-loop therapy to 16 out of 100 after activation, with daily detections correlating strongly (r = 0.68) with naturalistic emotional stress.

In Scangos et al. (Jan 2021 Nature Medicine), identical intracranial stimulation parameters produced opposite mood effects depending on whether the patient's baseline brain network was in a low-arousal vs hyper-aroused state, explaining why fixed continuous DBS trials like Holtzheimer et al. (2017 Lancet Psychiatry) struggled.

Effective white-matter tractography and evoked potential mapping proved that right amygdala and right VC/VS formed a tightly coupled structural-functional subnetwork with a 25–40 ms directional signal latency.

Alagapan et al. (2023 Nature) further demonstrated in a 10-patient cohort that intracranial electrophysiological biomarkers can predict clinical relapse weeks before behavioral depression scores worsen.
